design_rationale: Participants were explicitly randomly assigned to exercise or wait-list using a programmed SAS random-number function in blocks of four.

domain_judgments.rationale: The sequence was appropriately generated with SAS block randomization and assigned by a separate author, but concealment until irrevocable enrollment is not clearly described and several baseline outcome measures favored the wait-list group.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The subjects in the present study were randomly and blindly assigned by author K.S. to either an exercise group (n = 40) or a wait-list (reference) group (n = 41) by means of a random block design.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants necessarily knew whether they exercised or waited, creating potential expectation-related deviations, although adherence was high, no competing treatment was reported, and intention-to-treat analysis was stated.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The subjects were asked to report if competing treatment was given, but none reported such treatment... In the exercise group 93% fully adhered to the exercise programme... The intention-to-treat approach was followed.

domain_judgments.rationale: Follow-up and item completeness were high in both groups, with only about 1% partial non-response, making material bias from missing outcomes unlikely despite simple prior-observation imputation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: In the exercise group 93% participated in all follow-up visits and in the reference group 90%... Data loss owing to partial non-response (missing data in returned questionnaires and protocols) was 1%.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary pain outcomes were participant-reported and elicited by an observer who knew allocation and also delivered exercise instructions, so both participants' expectations and unblinded assessment procedures could plausibly influence the measured treatment effect.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The same observer did all measurements. Since the observer also gave instructions about the exercise no blinded data collection was possible.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although the trial was registered and pain was identified as primary, registration appears potentially retrospective and the report used multiple pain measures, time points, crude and adjusted models, backward covariate elimination, and responder analyses without a clearly reported prespecified analysis plan.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: To avoid analysis model overload, non-significant covariates were excluded by backward elimination... Moreover, adjusted mean values across the study period were used for statistical testing to provide optimum statistical power.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high, driven by the primary subjective pain outcomes being measured under unavoidable participant awareness and by the same unblinded observer who instructed the intervention. Additional concerns arise from incompletely described allocation concealment, expectation-related deviations, and analytic flexibility.

design_rationale: Participants were explicitly randomized to three groups using an off-site computer-generated sequence in permuted blocks, with telephone allocation concealment.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation sequence was computer-generated in permuted blocks, held off site, and implemented by concealed telephone allocation, with no important baseline imbalance suggesting failure of randomization.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: We randomised participants by telephone via concealed allocation... The randomisation sequence (kept off site and drawn up by a computerised random number generator in permuted blocks of six) and group allocation were kept concealed from all study personnel...

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and treating clinicians could not be blinded, and additional treatment differed substantially by randomized group, although use of blinded intention-to-treat analysis limits concern.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Wait and see participants (34/62, 55%) sought significantly more not per protocol treatment than physiotherapy participants (13/63, 21%)... Injection participants sought significantly more not per protocol treatment than physiotherapy participants.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome availability was high and balanced at 52 weeks (62/67, 65/65, and 63/66), and the analysis was conducted on an intention-to-treat basis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: We did statistical analyses on a blinded, intention to treat basis... [At 52 weeks:] wait and see 56/62; physiotherapy 59/63 [and injection 44/65].

domain_judgments.rationale: Validated outcomes were measured consistently and assessor-based outcomes were blinded, but key participant-reported outcomes such as global improvement could be influenced by unavoidable knowledge of treatment assignment, and assessor blinding was imperfect.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: At 52 weeks, the blinded assessor correctly guessed the allocated treatment in 101/198 (51%) cases... four participants... inadvertently revealed their group allocation.

domain_judgments.rationale: No prospective registration or prespecified statistical analysis plan is reported, and multiple primary outcomes, time points, analyses, and a post hoc subgroup analysis create scope for selective reporting despite explicit primary endpoints and multiplicity adjustment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary end points for the trial were six weeks (short term) and 52 weeks (long term)... we decided to compare treatments at each time point... with significance set at 0.01... We did a post hoc subgroup analysis...

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is judged some concerns. Randomization, concealment, retention, and intention-to-treat analysis were strong, but differential non-protocol treatment, participant-reported outcomes in an unblinded trial, imperfect assessor blinding, and lack of reported prospective registration or an analysis plan introduce concerns.

design_rationale: Participants were explicitly allocated to three treatment groups by a researcher using a computer program with a minimization strategy after consent and baseline assessment.

domain_judgments.rationale: The sequence was generated by computer-assisted minimization after consent and baseline assessment, allocation concealment was explicitly claimed, and baseline characteristics were reported as well matched.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: After retrieval of informed consent, patients were included in the trial by the medical doctor (GK) and subsequently randomized by a researcher (PS) using a computer program with minimization strategy for the duration of complaints.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and treating therapists could not be blinded, 17 participants violated the treatment protocol, and some received additional treatment, although rates were similar and both intention-to-treat and per-protocol analyses gave similar results.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: For the per-protocol analysis, a total of 17 patients who violated the treatment protocol were excluded. Similar results were found when compared to the intention-to-treat analysis.

domain_judgments.rationale: Only four of 180 randomized participants were lost by 6 weeks and total dropout remained below 6% at one year, making material bias from missing outcomes unlikely.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The dropout rate was less than 6% after 1-year follow-up and thus kept to a minimum.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome measurement was standardized and the assessor was effectively blinded, but several principal outcomes were patient-reported and participants necessarily knew whether they received a brace, physical therapy, or both, so their reports could have been influenced by treatment knowledge.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The blinded assessor was asked to guess the allocation of the 176 patients at 6 weeks follow-up and was correct for 73 (41%) patients (κ = 0.12) and was never certain of his guess.

domain_judgments.rationale: The paper identifies a primary endpoint and says subgroup analyses were preplanned, but no protocol or prespecified analysis plan is provided and numerous outcomes, time points, pairwise contrasts, and both intention-to-treat and per-protocol analyses allowed reporting flexibility.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Main outcome measures were success rate, severity of complaints, pain, disability, and satisfaction. Data were analyzed using both intention-to-treat and per-protocol analyses.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is some concerns. Randomization, assessor blinding, and outcome completeness were strong, but the open-label behavioral treatments could influence patient-reported outcomes, protocol deviations occurred, and the absence of an accessible prespecified analysis plan leaves potential for selective reporting among many outcomes and analyses.

design_rationale: Participants were explicitly assigned after baseline by drawing one of two folded notes from a container, within a stratified randomized block design.

domain_judgments.rationale: The sequence was generated by participants drawing folded notes after baseline and groups were balanced, but the report does not explain safeguards ensuring that the notes were indistinguishable or that allocation remained concealed and unpredictable throughout each stratified block.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Allocation after the baseline examination was randomized by each subject picking from a container one of two folded notes showing either a ‘one’ (exercise group) or a ‘two’ (control group).

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants were masked to which component was under investigation and adherence was reported as over 70%, but they necessarily knew whether they performed exercises, and the per-protocol analysis excluded five randomized participants rather than estimating an intention-to-treat effect.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The subjects did not know whether such minimal intervention or the additional eccentric training was under investigation... As with the main outcomes, data were approached as per protocol.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data were unavailable for 5 of 42 randomized participants (12%), with similar attrition across groups and reported reasons, but exclusions included intervention-related inconvenience or increased pain and no analysis adequately ruled out outcome-dependent missingness.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Thirty-seven (88%) completed the mid-intervention follow-up at week 3 and 37 (88%) did so at the end... Two felt inconvenience or exaggerated pain when using the forearm band... there were no follow-up data for drop-outs and the analysis was therefore conducted as per protocol.

domain_judgments.rationale: The strength outcomes were measured identically in both groups with specified instruments and protocols, but assessor blinding is not reported and the pain-limited stopping rules permit assessor or participant expectations to influence measurements despite partial participant masking.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Subjects were instructed to squeeze the dynamometer slowly as hard as they could or until they felt discomfort... The trial was immediately interrupted either when the wrist angle changed or when the subject felt discomfort.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was registered and outcomes were identified as main or secondary, but the report provides no protocol or prespecified statistical analysis plan timing/details to exclude selective choice among multiple time points, strength measurements, and analyses.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The study was registered in the database ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT00975442).

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is judged as some concerns. Concerns arise from incompletely documented allocation concealment, per-protocol exclusion of 12% of randomized participants, possible influence of treatment awareness on pain-limited outcomes without reported assessor blinding, and insufficient information to exclude selective reporting.

design_rationale: The study explicitly used a predetermined allocation sequence generated from a random-numbers table, with assignments placed in opaque numbered envelopes.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation sequence was generated using a random-numbers table with balanced blocks and concealed in opaque numbered envelopes, and the modest baseline imbalances are plausible in this small trial.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The numbers were issued in a predetermined random sequence using a block size of 24 and generated by the use of a random numbers table... The treatment group details were then sealed in a series of opaque numbered envelopes.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and providers could not plausibly be blinded to observation, injection, or physiotherapy, and the analysis was based on available follow-up data rather than an intention-to-treat approach, with substantial differential attrition in physiotherapy groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Another limitation of our study was the relatively high 10 of 24 (41%) drop out rate of patients from the two groups who had physiotherapy as part of their treatment regime [physiotherapy alone (n = 5) and physiotherapy plus steroid injection (n = 5)].

domain_judgments.rationale: Overall and differential missingness was substantial, with 41% lost from physiotherapy-containing groups, and the authors considered missingness likely related to better pain and function, making outcome-dependent missingness plausible.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: There is a strong likelihood that patients who failed to return for follow up would have better function and less pain, although we cannot be really sure as to the reasons.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although the primary outcome was appropriate and measured consistently, the research physiotherapist performed follow-up assessments and likely knew treatment assignment, while pain-limited grip strength and patient-reported outcomes could be influenced by that knowledge.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Outcome assessments were performed by the research physiotherapist before randomisation and 7 weeks after the actual start of the treatment.

domain_judgments.rationale: No preregistration or prespecified analysis plan is reported, and several outcome measures and analytical choices were available, although the paper identifies the primary outcome and reports all listed outcomes.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary outcome measure, pain free grip strength (PFGS), was measured in kilograms.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high because substantial, differential, plausibly outcome-related missing data threaten the estimated effects, and unblinded assessment of pain-sensitive and patient-reported outcomes could have influenced measurements. Concerns also remain about deviations/available-case analysis and selective reporting without a prespecified protocol.

design_rationale: Assignment was deterministic by medical registry number (odd numbers to Group 1 and even numbers to Group 2), which is a quasi-random allocation rule rather than a genuinely random sequence.

domain_judgments.rationale: Registry-number parity was plausibly unrelated to prognosis and measured baseline characteristics did not differ significantly, but the analysis was unadjusted and comparability was only assessed for a limited set of measured factors, leaving residual confounding possible.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Ninety-four patients were consented, enrolled and randomized to one of two groups according to their medical registry number, with odd numbered registrants enrolled in Group 1 and even numbered registrants in Group 2.

domain_judgments.domain_name: Bias due to selection of participants into the study
domain_judgments.rationale: The reported comparative analysis excluded many participants after intervention assignment for post-baseline events, including treatment escalation, dropout, and failure to complete therapy, so inclusion in the analyzed cohort could depend on both intervention experience and outcome prognosis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A total of 35 patients (37%) were either excluded or lost to follow up at 12 months. Twenty-five patients were excluded for a variety of reasons including going on to have a steroid injection or surgery, desiring to drop out of study, failing to complete the full therapy program, or discovery of comorbidities post consent.

domain_judgments.rationale: The two intervention conditions were clearly defined at assignment, with strengthening explicitly added only to Group 1, making intervention misclassification unlikely.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Group 1 consisted of patients that received all components of the program with the addition of eccentric strengthening. Group 2 received the program but not the strengthening component.

domain_judgments.domain_name: Bias due to deviations from intended interventions
domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and treating therapists necessarily knew whether strengthening was prescribed, adherence and contamination were not reported, and the analysis excluded participants who failed to complete therapy or received injections or surgery rather than retaining them according to initial assignment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Twenty-five patients were excluded for a variety of reasons including going on to have a steroid injection or surgery, desiring to drop out of study, failing to complete the full therapy program, or discovery of comorbidities post consent.

domain_judgments.rationale: Only 59 of 94 assigned participants contributed complete or near-complete 52-week data, with differential retention between groups and no appropriate missing-data analysis demonstrating robustness to informative missingness.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Group 1 yielded 38 participants who were able to be followed for the full 52 weeks with complete or near complete data. Group 2 yielded 21. A total of 35 patients (37%) were either excluded or lost to follow up at 12 months.

domain_judgments.rationale: Pain and function were subjective self-reported outcomes, and participants knew whether they were receiving the additional strengthening component, so outcome reports could have been influenced by intervention knowledge despite use of validated scales and common assessment methods.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Outcome measures of 1) pain at rest and with activity and 2) QuickDASH scores were obtained at initial, 6 and 12 week visits. The same outcomes were collected by phone or email at 24 and 52 weeks after initiation of therapy.

domain_judgments.domain_name: Bias in selection of the reported result
domain_judgments.rationale: No preregistered protocol or prespecified statistical analysis plan is reported, and multiple outcomes and time points created opportunities for selective analysis or reporting, although the main stated outcomes appear to be reported across all planned follow-ups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Our primary outcome measure was pain at rest and pain with activity; our secondary measure was level of functional impairment as measured by the QuickDASH. Outcome measurements were assessed at baseline, 6, 12, 24 and 52 weeks post initiation of therapy.

overall_summary: Overall ROBINS-I risk is serious, driven by post-assignment exclusions and substantial missing outcome data, departures from an intention-to-treat effect estimate, and unblinded self-reported outcomes. Clear intervention definitions and broadly similar measured baseline characteristics do not overcome these limitations.

design_rationale: Participants were explicitly allocated after baseline by drawing subject numbers from an opaque urn, with the draw performed by a research assistant who had no further involvement in the study.

domain_judgments.rationale: Allocation was generated by an independent assistant drawing identifiers from an opaque urn and was concealed until distribution was complete, but the authors question the urn method and a marked baseline imbalance in symptom duration remained after post-randomization attrition.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A number assigned to each subject was placed in an opaque urn. A research assistant with no further implication in this study has drawn numbers to form the 2 groups.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and the treating clinician were unblinded, and three randomized control participants were excluded rather than analyzed in their assigned group, so the analysis was not intention-to-treat and could materially bias this very small trial.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The possibility of an intention-to-treat analysis was evaluated, but because the missing data were too important, the subjects lost to follow-up were removed from the analysis.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data were unavailable for 3 of 30 randomized participants (10%), all from the control group, and their post-assignment exclusion created a significant imbalance in symptom duration that the authors acknowledged limited treatment-effect inference.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Three subjects from the control group could not come back after the group assignment, so their data were not used because we only had their baseline data.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although PRTEE, VAS, and grip strength are appropriate and were scheduled similarly across groups, outcomes were either participant-reported in an unblinded trial or measured by the unblinded clinician who delivered both interventions, making differential assessment plausible.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The clinician responsible of the study, a chiropractor completing a masters' degree in kinesiology, collected and managed all the data. He also provided all the treatment to the experimental group and the advice to the control group.

domain_judgments.rationale: The paper prospectively identifies PRTEE as primary and VAS and grip strength as secondary and reports them across stated time points, but no protocol or prospective trial registration is provided to rule out selection among analyses or measurements.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary outcome assessment was the PRTEE. The 2 secondary measurements were the PFG and the VAS.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high, driven by differential post-randomization loss of three control participants without intention-to-treat analysis and by unblinded participant-reported and clinician-measured outcomes. Concerns about the randomization method, baseline imbalance, and absence of a prespecified public protocol further reduce confidence.

design_rationale: This was a parallel-group randomized clinical trial using a computer-generated allocation sequence, with participants assigned to isometric exercise or wait-and-see after baseline assessment.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation sequence was computer-generated by an independent researcher, allocation was concealed until after baseline measurement using opaque envelopes, and reported baseline characteristics were broadly comparable.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A computer-generated randomisation sequence was performed by a researcher not involved in data collection... Following baseline measurements, participants were randomly allocated using concealed opaque envelopes to either the exercise or wait-and-see group.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants necessarily knew whether they were prescribed exercise, and although adherence was high, co-interventions occurred and there was no participant blinding; however, co-intervention use was similar and intention-to-treat analyses were used.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Statistical analyses were performed on an intention-to-treat basis... Use of co-interventions was similar between groups.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data were available for essentially all randomized participants, with only one exercise participant missing two primary outcome measurements and all participants contributing GROC data.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Follow-up at 8 weeks was completed by 39 (98%) of 40 participants... a GROC score was obtained via telephone.

domain_judgments.rationale: Measures were administered consistently and the follow-up assessor was blinded, but key patient-reported outcomes such as PRTEE and GROC could be influenced by participants' unavoidable knowledge of treatment assignment; additionally, two thermode sizes were used for thermal thresholds.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Outcome measures were collected at baseline and at the 8-week follow-up time point by an assessor blinded to treatment allocation.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was registered and primary outcomes and principal analyses were described, but the supplied report does not provide a protocol or prospective analysis plan sufficient to rule out selection among multiple outcome definitions and analyses, including alternative GROC dichotomizations and per-protocol analyses.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The trial was registered in the Australian New Zealand Clinical Trial [Registry]... Sensitivity analyses of the GROC dichotomisation were performed... and on a per-protocol basis.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is some concerns. Randomization and retention were strong, but lack of participant blinding could affect deviations and patient-reported outcomes, and the available registration information does not fully exclude selective reporting among alternative outcome definitions or analyses.

design_rationale: Participants were explicitly allocated to intervention or control using a predetermined random-number sequence in blocks of four, with assignments placed in sealed envelopes opened after consent.

domain_judgments.rationale: The sequence was generated in advance from random numbers and concealed in sealed envelopes opened after consent, but opacity and sequential handling were not reported and one notable baseline imbalance in education was observed.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Randomization to intervention or control was performed in advance by the project coordinator in blocks of four according to a predetermined random sequence of numbers, and was supplied to each general practice in sealed envelopes, which were opened by the GP after eligible cases had signed an informed consent form.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and clinicians were unblinded, control participants commonly received exercise advice overlapping with the intervention, intervention compliance was low, and the analyzed cohort excluded randomized participants who did not receive the intervention rather than clearly following intention-to-treat.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The power of the study was reduced by exercise being encouraged by GPs in the control group also (44%), and by low compliance in the intervention group.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data were missing for a minority of randomized participants, and the investigators substituted 6-month outcomes for missing 12-month outcomes without evidence that missingness could not bias results.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: In order to increase power, the scores of overall improvement for 12 cases registered at 6 months but missing at 1 yr were included in the analysis. The same was done for 10 cases with regard to a 50% reduction in pain score.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcomes were subjective patient-reported pain and global improvement, and because participants could not be blinded, knowledge of assignment and the intervention's reassuring information could plausibly influence their reports despite identical questionnaire procedures.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Due to the design, no blinding to treatment could be done. The primary outcome assessment was done independently, based on patient self-reports in follow-up questionnaires.

domain_judgments.rationale: No prospective registration or prespecified statistical analysis plan is reported, and several time points, outcome operationalizations, and analytical choices—including dichotomization and substituting 6-month for 12-month observations—created scope for selective reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary outcome measures were self-reported overall development of the condition reported in follow-up questionnaires at 3, 6 and 12 months after inclusion in the trial... As an alternative measure of outcome, we used a reduction of at least 50% in a combined pain and function score.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high, driven by substantial deviations from intended interventions (control-group contamination, low intervention compliance, and exclusion of some randomized participants) and by unblinded measurement of subjective self-reported outcomes. Additional concerns arise from incompletely described allocation concealment, missing-outcome handling, and lack of prespecified reporting information.

design_rationale: Participants were explicitly assigned to three treatment groups using a computerized random-number generator, with stratified permuted blocks and allocation through opaque sealed envelopes after baseline assessment.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation sequence was computer-generated with stratified permuted blocks and concealed in opaque sealed envelopes opened only after final eligibility determination and baseline assessment; minor baseline imbalances were examined and had little effect on results.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: We used a computerised random number generator to draw up an allocation schedule... The assignment of patients... took place after final selection by the research physiotherapist and baseline assessment. An administrative assistant allocated interventions via opaque sealed envelopes marked according to the allocation schedule.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and providers could not be blinded, and substantial post-intervention additional treatment differed across groups, although cointerventions were discouraged during the initial 6 weeks and the principal analysis used intention-to-treat.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Only 14 (24%) patients in the wait-and-see group received additional treatment for elbow complaints during the 1-year follow-up, compared with 39 (63%) in the injection group and 52 (81%) in the physiotherapy group... The principal analysis was done on an intention-to-treat basis.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data were nearly complete, with only two withdrawals among 185 randomized participants and isolated missed assessments, making material bias from missing outcomes unlikely.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Furthermore, drop-out rate was kept to a minimum (<2%, 2).

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome instruments and assessment schedules were appropriate and consistent, but key outcomes were patient-reported in an unblinded trial and assessor blinding was sometimes compromised, creating potential for knowledge of treatment to influence measurements.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: At 6 weeks, the research physiotherapists correctly guessed the allocated treatment in 94 of 181 patients... A slip of the tongue by the patient disclosed allocation in 17 instances.

domain_judgments.rationale: The paper states that a protocol existed and reports prespecified assessment times and outcomes, but no registration or prespecified statistical analysis plan is provided to exclude selective choice among multiple outcomes, time points, and analyses.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The medical ethics committee of Vrije Universiteit Medical Centre approved our protocol.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is some concerns. Randomization and outcome completeness were strong, but lack of participant blinding, differential additional treatments, partial loss of assessor blinding, and insufficient information to rule out selective reporting raise concerns.

design_rationale: This was an explicitly randomized three-arm controlled trial using a computerized variable-block randomization schedule and concealed allocation by an independent research assistant.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation sequence was computer-generated with variable block sizes, assignment was concealed through an independent assistant contacted only after enrollment, and reported baseline differences did not raise a clear concern about randomization failure.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A computerised randomisation schedule was prepared by an independent researcher (ML), using numeric block randomisation with variable block size... Only then was an independent research assistant contacted, who, by consulting the previously prepared randomisation schedule, allocated the patient to one of three treatments ensuring concealed allocation.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants could not be blinded to physiotherapy versus wait-and-see, and additional treatment was permitted and differed for additional physiotherapy, although adherence was generally good and the primary analysis was described as intention-to-treat.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The patients were not blinded to the physiotherapy treatment, and that may have influenced outcome... there was significantly more use of additional physiotherapy in the CI with physiotherapy group compared to the placebo injection with physiotherapy group.

domain_judgments.rationale: Primary outcome completion was high at 89%, but 11% were lost and the unadjusted primary analysis assumed all missing participants were treatment failures without reporting sensitivity analyses establishing robustness to plausible missing outcomes.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The trial was completed in June 2013, with 157 patients (89 %) completing the primary outcome at 52 weeks follow-up... assuming those lost to follow-up had no success as outcome.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome was an appropriate self-reported improvement scale applied identically across groups, but participants knew whether they received physiotherapy and the steroid arm may have been partly unblinded, so knowledge of intervention could influence this subjective outcome.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary outcome measures were the patients’ evaluations of improvement... The patients were not blinded to the physiotherapy treatment... For CI with physiotherapy, correct treatment was guessed in 61 % of cases.

domain_judgments.rationale: A prospectively registered trial and published protocol were reported, but the text does not establish that the detailed GEE covariate-selection strategy and all eligible outcome analyses were prespecified, leaving some potential for selective analysis among numerous outcomes and time points.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Trial registration: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT00826462... Univariate GEE logistic regression models were fitted to our primary outcome... to identify significant covariates. Only these covariates were used in our final models.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is some concerns. Randomization and concealment were strong, but the subjective primary outcome could be influenced by incomplete participant blinding, 11% attrition was handled using an unverified failure assumption, post-randomization additional treatment occurred, and prespecification of the detailed adjusted analyses was not fully established.

design_rationale: The Methods explicitly state that patients were randomized to three treatment arms using Randomizer software with allocation concealment.

domain_judgments.rationale: A software-generated randomization procedure with allocation concealment was explicitly reported, and the reported age and sex distributions did not show clear baseline imbalance.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Patients were randomized with allocation concealment using Randomizer→ software by MEDSHARING

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and treating therapists could not plausibly be blinded to these physical interventions, concomitant analgesic use was not evaluated, and the report does not explicitly describe adherence, protocol deviations, or an intention-to-treat analysis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Finally, this study did not evaluate the use of concomitant medications, such as analgesics.

domain_judgments.rationale: Results are presented for all 52 included participants, but incomplete data were an exclusion criterion and the timing and extent of any post-randomization exclusions or attrition are not reported, so bias from missing outcomes cannot be ruled out.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The exclusion criteria were as follows: ... or incomplete data.

domain_judgments.rationale: The outcome evaluator was blinded and measurement schedules were common across groups, but pain and function were self-reported by participants aware of treatment assignment, and the German translation of PRTEE was unvalidated.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The physician (corresponding author) evaluating the patient outcomes was blinded to the patient groups.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was registered retrospectively years after ethics approval, multiple primary and secondary outcomes, time points, and SF-36 subscores were available, and some results were omitted as data not shown, creating substantial scope for selective outcome or analysis reporting without a prospective protocol.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Trial registration: German Clinical Trial Register: DRKS, trial registration number: 00021137, date of registration: 24/03/2020 (retrospectively registered)

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high, driven by high risk in selection of the reported result because registration was retrospective and numerous outcomes, time points, and analyses were available. Additional concerns arise from lack of participant blinding, unassessed concomitant medication and adherence, unclear handling of incomplete data, and participant-reported outcomes.
